rounds.text: Creative Newtech Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line compounding, driven by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 39% [E14] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 45% [E17], significantly outperforming sector medians [E66, E67]. This fundamental outperformance relative to the stock's historical 5-year price growth of 24% points to a classic fundamentals-led divergence where business value has outpaced market pricing [E20, E52]. Valuation mechanics further support a strong upside thesis, with a discounted cash flow model establishing an intrinsic value that leaves a massive 50.9% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 1,082 [E41, E42]. The reverse DCF implies that today's market price expects a modest 8.2% earnings growth, which is easily eclipsed by the base case expectation of 18.0% growth [E43]. Operational quality and efficiency stand well above sector norms, highlighted by an ROA of 7.86% versus a sector benchmark of 2.92% [E8], an ROCE of 14.89% against 6.82% [E10], and an institutional money flow showing positive accumulation through rising domestic and foreign holdings [E38, E39, E40]. Furthermore, the company has actively strengthened its balance sheet by reducing borrowings down to Rs 194 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 324 Cr a year prior [E35], while rules-based screening awards the stock a high-confidence BUY score of 92 out of 100 [E58]. Conceded: the business faces negative operating and free cash flows totaling Rs -272 Cr and Rs -275 Cr respectively for March 2026 alongside an extension in debtor days [E31, E32, E57].

The most alarming risk in Creative Newtech Ltd lies in its catastrophic cash generation failure, where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -272 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -275 Cr in March 2026, producing a dismal cash conversion ratio of -3.89x against reported profits [E30, E32]. This severe cash drain is compounded by ballooning working capital pressures, evidenced by debtor days surging significantly from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E57]. Furthermore, the company trades at a clear valuation premium over its peers, sporting a P/E of 22.35x and a P/B of 4.53x against sector benchmarks of 17.56x and 1.38x respectively, alongside an elevated EV/EBITDA of 16.79x versus the sector's 10.27x [E6, E7, E11]. Investors also face severe structural volatility, as demonstrated by an annualized volatility of 52.8% and a worst peak-to-trough historical drawdown of -51.3% [E49, E50]. Growth momentum shows explicit signs of exhaustion, with screen warnings indicating that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E63] and recent price growth outpacing profit growth by 30%, which signals that market expectations have sprinted far ahead of operational delivery [E53]. Conceded: [E14, E16, E19, E56].

Conceded: [E30, E32, E57]. While cash flows show a temporary deficit in March 2026, the company's fundamental efficiency ratios vastly outperform sector benchmarks, with an ROA of 7.86% versus 2.92% and an ROCE of 14.89% against 6.82% [E8, E10]. The premium multiples cited by the bear are fully justified by stellar operational velocity, including a 5-year compounded profit growth of 45% and TTM sales expansion of 36%, both crushing sector medians [E14, E16, E17, E66, E67]. Furthermore, balance sheet health is actively improving as borrowings dropped sharply to Rs 194 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 324 Cr a year prior, dispelling fears of structural balance sheet distress [E35]. Institutional confidence remains robust with positive money flow and increased holdings from both domestic and foreign institutions [E38, E39, E40], while rules-based screens score the equity a high-confidence 92 out of 100 on strong top- and bottom-line momentum [E58, E59, E60].

Conceded: [E8, E10, E14, E16, E17, E35, E38, E39, E40, E58, E59, E60]. While those efficiency and growth metrics are present, they completely ignore the alarming cash burn where operating cash flow and free cash flow collapsed to negative ₹ 272 Cr and negative ₹ 275 Cr respectively [E30, E32]. That severe cash drain directly undermines the reported profit expansion and coincides with debtor days worsening significantly from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E57]. Furthermore, the claim that premium multiples are justified ignores the bearish reality that the stock trades at a P/E of 22.35x and EV/EBITDA of 16.79x, both carrying steep premiums over sector benchmarks of 17.56x and 10.27x [E6, E11]. Institutional support cannot insulate investors from the rules-based warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E63]. Finally, anyone buying on past momentum must contend with a brutal historical record featuring an annualised volatility of 52.8% and a maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% [E49, E50].
